findings.note: At 4946dd01, QuotaCooldowns.cs:34 and QuotaCooldowns.Round.cs:8 both declare `sealed partial class QuotaCooldowns` to keep each file under 400 lines, which coding-style.md:25 forbids; 6927d17b extracted the internal class QuotaRound to fix it.
The plan's gate record (§11, second gate, F0) rejected exactly this size cap, because keys exist only per configured row until their reset and a cap with eviction could un-park a really spent row.

QuotaCooldowns.Round.cs:50-56 does await each key's probe in turn, so wait times add up per key (fixed with Task.WhenAll in QuotaRound.cs at 6927d17b), but ten unknown-family keys in one round is an inflated scenario.
AgyQuotaGroups only maps a model to its quota key and routes nothing; plan D3 sets this exact `3p` table row and says it exists for GPT-OSS and for a row somebody configures against vendor-routing.

The dictionary at QuotaCooldowns.cs:115 is a local working table built and consumed inside WriteUnderLock; no shared or input object is mutated, so this is a pedantic reading of the immutability rule.
QuotaCooldownFile (QuotaCooldowns.cs:266) is an internal serialization DTO, not a public contract, so the doctrine's public-contract rule does not apply.

Every reviewer runtime passes itself as Adapter (KimiRuntime.cs:126 via Bound(settings), AntigravityRuntime.cs:72, ClaudeRuntime.cs:114, ReviewerRuntime.cs:689), and plan D5 prescribes `Invocation.Adapter.QuotaKeyOf(Invocation.Model)`.
PanelService builds one QuotaCooldowns and passes that same instance to RoundEngine, so there is no second instance; reading the file on every CanRun with no cache is what plan D4 decided.
Plan D3 requires one explicit measured table, with an unknown family getting its own key and no gauge-based parking; the gate rejected prefix or dynamic matching (§11, second gate, F4).
JsonDocument.TryParseValue at AgyError.cs:35-36 reads only the first JSON value and ignores what follows, JsonException is caught at :46, and the multi-line shape is intentional (commit 4946dd01).
The caller owns Hold.Taken's FileStream (HeldFile.TakenByDotNet), so disposing it at QuotaCooldowns.cs:107 is exactly how the lock is released; there is no double dispose.
Plan D5 says cancellation reaches the caller; AfterRoundAsync catches OperationCanceledException (Round.cs:20), and no other caller of ReadResetAsync exists.
Plan D4 explicitly decides 'read on every CanRun, no cache' for a file under 16 KiB, so the caching it asks for goes against the spec.
QuotaCooldowns.Round.cs:50-52 awaits MoveAsync key by key, so N hanging probes cost up to N×30 s; 6927d17b moved to Task.WhenAll (QuotaRound.cs MovesAsync).
AgyError.Parse runs only on a failed launch's short stderr, so the allocations are negligible micro-optimisation noise.
Plan D3 and story 2 place exactly this table, AgyQuotaGroups, in AgyQuotaReport.cs, and no other model-family seam makes quota decisions.
The plan's gate rejected an enforced 16 KiB cap (§11, second gate, F0); the bound in §8 is a projection kept by expiry, not a write-time check.
Plan D5 puts the awaited AfterRoundAsync between RunAllAsync and the summary on purpose, so that the round says what it parked (RoundEngine.cs:442).
The invocation's model comes from the same provider.Model (RosterBuilder.cs:529 `Model = provider.Model`), and KeyOf maps an empty model to DefaultModel on both sides, so the keys cannot differ.

The unlocked Standing only skips taking the lock when nothing stands; a park another process writes later comes from a newer refusal and should win, and the locked Remove stays idempotent (QuotaRound.cs MoveAsync).
Plan D1 says `limited.Spent ?? RateLimit.Hopeless(limited.Reason)` with 'the ResetOutlasts half unchanged', which is exactly BoundedScheduler.cs:681.
Both the park and the CanRun lookup derive the key from the same configured model string, and known families match case-insensitively (AgyQuotaReport.cs:40), so no casing mismatch arises in practice.
TimeLeft (PanelService.cs) reads the clock again after StandingFor, so it can print '0 min' or a negative value in a sub-millisecond window, but nothing throws and 'Major' overstates it.
ExitReason passes the line through VendorReason.Written, which is Redaction.SafeText with the safety cap — the product's one redactor (VendorReason.cs:31).
Plan D4 decides no cache and a read on every decision, over a file of a few KB; this repeats R1#12.
This is allocation micro-optimisation on the failure-only stderr path, a repeat of R1#14.
This duplicates R2#7: Math.Ceiling of any positive remainder gives at least '1 min', so '0 min' or a negative value appears only when the second clock read lands past untilUtc.

missed: RefusalOf requires RateLimit.Hopeless(reason) even for an undecided agy refusal (Spent == null), so an agy RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED whose message lacks a 'spent' word is never probed, although D5 says that for agy the gauge decides the undecided case.

ExcludedFrom calls CanRun and then ReasonFor, which reads the file again; a cooldown that lapses between the two reads leaves CoolingOrCredentialReason falling through to a credential sentence for a row whose credentials are fine.
summary: Only three findings hold up and are worth acting on: the `partial` split and the serial /quota probes (both fixed in the next commit), plus a cosmetic TimeLeft edge reported twice. Most of the rest contradicts the plan's explicit decisions (no cache, no size cap, the explicit table, the awaited probe, Hopeless unchanged) or misreads the code (the Adapter is never null, there is no second instance, and the stderr line is already redacted).
